text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states the air suspension irons out bumps and manhole covers well even on 22-inch wheels. Reviewer measured a very quiet cabin, 62.9 dB(A) at 130 km/h, quieter than a Mercedes S-Class. Reviewer states the materials feel high quality and pleasantly soft. Reviewer measured 19.6 kWh/100 km and about 513 km range in the ADAC cycle (WLTP 667 km). Reviewer measured up to 296 kW and an average 168 kW from 10-80%, about 24 minutes for roughly 379 km. Reviewer states legroom front and rear is generous, even for very tall occupants. Reviewer rates rear visibility as very poor because of the small rear window; manoeuvring without the reversing camera is problematic and the optional digital mirror is not ideal for glasses wearers. Reviewer criticises a centre console without buttons; lights and mirror or steering-column adjustment run via the display, which is highly distracting, and the steering wheel buttons are unlit. Reviewer criticises the lack of separate switches for the rear windows as inappropriate for the price class. Reviewer criticises the transponder key in place of a proper remote key, with the smartphone as the alternative. Reviewer finds the electric, automatically extending door handles impractical. Reviewer measured 400 to 1,365 litres of boot space, only moderate for a 5 m saloon. Reviewer states the sloping C-pillar limits rear headroom for people over 1.90 m. Reviewer criticises AC charging at only 11 kW, so a full charge takes at least nine hours. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «wie eine rollende Sänfte» «mangelhaft» «mäßig»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states the 653 PS drivetrain performs on a par with Tesla, with 60-100 km/h in 3.2 s. Reviewer measured 20.4 kWh/100 km in the ADAC Ecotest (four of five stars), about 485 km range with the 100 kWh battery. Reviewer states 10-80% takes about 40 minutes even under ideal conditions, with 126 kW peak and 97 kW average, clearly below competitors. Reviewer highlights the robotic battery swap in about five minutes, with first German swap stations in Zusmarshausen, Hilden and Berlin. Reviewer states the air suspension lets the car glide calmly. Reviewer states the evasive-manoeuvre test was passed safely, with a sensitive and effective ESP. Reviewer states the steering feels indifferent and synthetic around centre, with too much assistance for European tastes. Reviewer states the assistance systems were surprisingly unreliable: sign recognition showed wrong limits, ACC braked for no reason and the lane assist intervened roughly. Reviewer states almost every function, even the hazard lights, is operated by touch, with a considerable distraction risk and a menu structure that is not intuitive. Reviewer states the NOMI assistant responds in a friendly way and reliably controls seat heating, massage and weather queries. Reviewer states rear knee room is very generous. Reviewer states the coupe-like roofline limits front headroom from about 1.90 m. Reviewer states the 365-litre boot is flat, deep and hard to access. Reviewer states the rear backrests cannot be folded because of the massage seats. Reviewer states buying the car outright including the battery is expensive, and NIO itself expects low demand for that option. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «erstaunlich unzuverlässig»

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer states the facelift rides much more comfortably than before, smoothing bumps without electronic dampers, though sharp edges are still felt. Reviewer states new double glazing clearly reduces cabin noise (66.2 dB(A) at 130 km/h). Reviewer found the test car's build quality flawless, a former weak point, with more padded and carpeted surfaces. Reviewer calls the two small indicator buttons on the steering wheel unintuitive and unsafe, especially when manoeuvring and leaving roundabouts. Reviewer criticises that the glovebox can only be opened via the touchscreen, part of a minimalism taken too far. Reviewer states the menus are intuitive after familiarisation and the screen responds quickly. Reviewer states the adaptive cruise control is unreliable, repeatedly braking for no apparent reason. Reviewer states the camera-only system without ultrasonic sensors cannot fully assist parking in the dark. Reviewer notes there is no conventional (non-adaptive) cruise control. Reviewer measured top-class consumption of 17.2 kWh/100 km (about 395 km) for the base car and about 470 km for the AWD. Reviewer states the charging curve drops quickly after the 173 kW peak; 10-80% took 31 minutes. Reviewer states Plug&Charge makes Supercharging very convenient. Reviewer states rear headroom limits passengers to about 1.90 m. Reviewer states rear visibility is heavily restricted, making the reversing camera practically indispensable. Reviewer considers the prices fair, saying a BMW i4 or comparable rivals are not available for the money.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer lists very good performance as a strength of the A6 Avant 2.0 TFSI e-hybrid quattro. Reviewer criticises high electric consumption (26.8 kWh/100 km incl. charging losses), giving 83 km of measured electric range from the 20.7 kWh net battery versus 104 km WLTP. Reviewer lists the lack of a DC fast-charging port as a weakness; the plug-in hybrid charges only by AC at up to 11 kW (about 150 minutes). Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «sehr gute Fahrleistungen» «hoher elektrischer Verbrauch» «kein Schnellladeanschluss»
